**Finding submitted: COMPLIANT** (confidence 0.89) — no redline proposed.

**What I checked.** I ran a full-text sweep for exclusivity formulations ("exclusive", "sole", "requirements from", "shall not … third party/competitor", "only", "all of Client's") and read the three planner-flagged sections in full: the licence grant (§2), Compensation (§5), and Client's covenants (§8).

**Why it's compliant.** The Agreement contains no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Mortgage Logic. §2(a) actually does better than silence — it grants a **non-exclusive** licence and affirmatively confirms that Client "is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system … to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink." The only limits on that freedom are non-infringement of TrueLink IP and existing confidentiality duties, neither of which restricts sourcing. This sits at the **preferred** position, not the fallback.

**Direction check on the other hits.** Three matches run in our favour or are irrelevant, so I did not flag them:
- p0054 — a *non-exclusive* licence of Credit Data **to** TrueLink (a grant by us, not a restraint on us).
- p0094 — an exclusive **forum** clause (venue, not dealing).
- The referenced Non-Competition Agreement — it *limits TrueLink's* use of Credit Data, i.e. exclusivity benefiting the Customer, which the rule expressly says is acceptable.

**One item noted in the rationale rather than redlined.** §3(i) says "Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface." That is the closest thing to a sole-source commitment in the document, and it's worth your awareness. I concluded it is not a rule breach because it is a narrow tie-in scoped to transactions we *voluntarily* route through the Interface — §2(a) leaves us free not to use the Interface at all and to buy credit reports elsewhere for any other loan. It is therefore not an all-requirements or exclusive-dealing covenant, and redlining it would risk double-flagging a commercial term better handled on its own merits.

**Practical watch-point for negotiation:** if TrueLink later proposes broadening §3(i) beyond Interface-routed transactions — e.g. striking the "through a System using the Interface" qualifier — that would convert it into a genuine requirements obligation and would then fail this rule. I'd resist that change or, at minimum, hold it to the fallback (defined category, 12 months, automatic exit on service-level failure).
